preamble: Labialization of the voiced velar fricative [ɣ] to the labiodental [v], typically next to back rounded vowels or in syllable codas after back vowels. It is attested in Hungarian, where Proto-Ugric intervocalic *ɣ surfaces as v in the stems of words like ló 'horse' (plural lovak), and in Karaim, where the Kipchak reflex of Proto-Turkic final *-g [ɣ] after back vowels is written v (tav 'mountain'); most sister Kipchak languages have [w] instead (Tatar, Kazakh taw).

examples.to: ló, stem lova- (plural lovak, accusative lovat)
examples.note: The intervocalic velar fricative surfaces as v in the vowel-final stem; the nominative ló shows the vocalized outcome.
Karaim has v where most Kipchak sisters have w (Tatar, Kazakh, Bashkir тау taw); the exact phonetic value of Karaim v here is not confirmed in the cited source.
